content.title: About
content.content: Italian Ice, No Sugar Added is a refreshing frozen dessert made from fruit puree, water and natural flavorings, without any added sugar. It has a light, snow‑like texture and a bright fruit taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Italian Ice originates from Italy, where it is known as “granita,” but it became a popular summer treat in the United States.
The lack of sugar makes it suitable for people monitoring blood glucose levels.
Unlike ice cream, Italian Ice contains no dairy, making it vegan‑friendly.
Flavors range from classic lemon and raspberry to exotic mango and passion fruit.
It is traditionally served in cups with a straw to enjoy the melting ice.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Without sugar and with minimal fat, Italian Ice is a low‑calorie dessert option.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: High water content helps maintain fluid balance on hot days.

items.title: Vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: Fruit puree provides vitamin C and other antioxidants that protect cells.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Some varieties contain small amounts of fruit fiber, which can aid digestion.

items.title: Diet‑friendly
items.content: Being sugar‑free and dairy‑free, it fits keto, vegan and gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Individuals may be allergic to specific fruits used in the recipe.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Some versions replace sugar with artificial sweeteners, which may not be suitable for everyone.

items.title: Cold shock
items.content: Consuming large amounts of a very cold product can cause tooth or throat discomfort.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Italian Ice straight from the freezer using a spoon or straw. It can be topped with fresh berries, mint, or a drizzle of natural sweetener if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep Italian Ice in an airtight container in the freezer. Over time ice crystals may form; briefly thaw in the fridge or at room temperature before serving.
